message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The gene that controls mane development is typically expressed in a dominant fashion—males that inherit the dominant allele will develop a mane, while females (who are heterozygous or homozygous for the recessive allele) do not. This dominant allele is responsible for the characteristic thick, dark mane that distinguishes male lions from females and juveniles.
